channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Florida mayor arrested on grand theft and fraud charges over COVID relief funds: AG
item.description: Kissimmee Mayor Jackie Espinosa is being charged with grand theft and organized scheme to defraud, according to Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier.

item.title: US and Israel drawing up plans to resume attacks on Iran post-election, sources say
item.description: The White House said Thursday that the U.S. will not resume attacks on Iran before the midterm elections on Nov. 3.

item.title: Scientists turn art detectives to date van Gogh's 'Starry Night' to actual sky from 1889
item.description: A team of South Korean researchers has put forward a new date for the night sky depicted in Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh's famed masterpiece "The Starry Night". Art historians have long assumed the stars were a product of the artist's fantasy or dated the scene to June 1889 based on the artist's location and other details, but astronomical details like the sliver crescent moon don't line up.

item.title: Ohio Gov. DeWine condemns Ramaswamy ad, calls on him to 'take it down'
item.description: "It's wrong to run this ad," DeWine said.

item.title: WATCH: Inside the North Carolina State Fair
item.description: ABC News' Leslie Lopez reports from Raleigh, where the North Carolina State Fair is underway and has already drawn hundreds of thousands of visitors.

item.title: Democrats sue Trump administration over alleged election pressure campaign
item.description: States say the administration's steps reflect federal overreach and are meant to sow distrust in the outcome of the election.

item.title: ‘No change’ in Russia’s attitude on war shown by deadly attacks, Zelensky says
item.description: Russia’s latest attacks on Ukraine show there has been “no real change” in Moscow’s attitude towards the war, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Thursday. The deadly strikes came just hours after Russian President Vladimir Putin told US envoy Steve Witkoff his country was ready to resume trilateral talks with Washington and Kyiv.

item.title: Ahead of US and Israeli elections, 3-day joint attack on Iran 'would not radically change conflict'
item.description: Jean-Emile Jammine is pleased to welcome Federico Donelli, Associate Professor of International Relations in the Department of Political and Social Sciences at the University of Trieste in Italy. Can another three days of military strikes achieve what eight months of confrontation have failed to deliver? Donelli challenges the assumption that a short, intensive offensive would necessarily produce a decisive political outcome. He argues, "the real question is whether military pressure is intended to constrain Iran's capacity, or to pressure Iran to sit on the table." And whether they can translate that capacity into a sustainable political outcome without provoking a wider regional crisis. Regardless, Donelli reminds us that "Iran still has leverage over the US."

item.title: French shopkeepers fear new looting in upcoming protests
item.description: In Paris, shopkeepers fear further losses ahead of a demonstration planned for next Saturday. After last weekend’s protests saw scenes of vandalism, some are considering closing their shops, while others plan to stay open.

item.title: WATCH: Critical debate showdowns in 2 key states ahead of midterm election
item.description: ABC News' Jay O'Brien reports on the high-stakes Senate debates in Michigan and Kansas as President Donald Trump stops in South Carolina to campaign for Republican candidates.

item.title: Judge orders Trump administration to halt noncitizen voting investigation in 9 states
item.description: A federal judge has ordered that President Donald Trump’s administration must halt investigations in nine states into whether noncitizens are registered to vote

item.title: Ukraine and Russia exchange strikes after US envoy visit to the Kremlin
item.description: Ukraine and Russia exchanged drone and missile strikes on Thursday, killing seven people in Ukraine, according to authorities. Moscow said it had intercepted 630 Ukrainian drones targeting the Russian capital. The strikes came hours after US envoy Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg. Witkoff said Moscow was ready to resume trilateral talks with Kyiv and Washington.

item.title: Georgia on Democrats’ minds: Powering up the Black vote to counter Trump's meddling
item.description: President Donald Trump's push to redistrict congressional maps and a Georgia state election law disproportionately affecting African Americans are aimed at diluting the power of the Black vote. Six decades after Atlanta was at the heart of the civil rights movement that granted Blacks in the southern states the right to vote, the community is fighting back.

item.title: Ethiopia-Eritrea: Is there a risk of a wider conflict?
item.description: Concerns are mounting as Ethiopia and Eritrea inch closer to war. With Ethiopia now having taken control of the border town of Zalambessa, the fear is that Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed will send his troops into Eritrea. In Perspective, we spoke to Martin Plaut, a senior research fellow at the Institute of Commonwealth Studies at the University of London.

item.title: French students demonstrate again, despite school holidays
item.description: The French "interfac" student movement organised new protests on Thursday, even though it is currently the school holidays in France. Student representatives are set to meet soon with Education Minister Edouard Geffray. Details by FRANCE 24's Ellen Gainsford.

item.title: Reports show US and Israel are planning new strikes on Iran
item.description: Reports claim that the US and Israel have ramped up military drills and planned new strikes in Iran, potentially targeting energy sites, drone facilities and missile arsenals. Details by FRANCE 24's correspondent in Jerusalem, Noga Tarnopolsky.

item.title: Italian truckers block roads to protest against soaring diesel prices
item.description: Italian truck drivers have been blocking refineries and key roads to protest against soaring diesel prices. Italy’s government has warned truckers blocking roads could face criminal penalties, as authorities move to clear demonstrations. Details by FRANCE 24's correspondent in Rome, Seema Gupta.

item.title: Iran live updates: IRGC Navy claims attacks on 4 vessels in Persian Gulf
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: Takeaways from the early vote in the 2026 midterms two weeks out
item.description: Early votes cast so far in the midterms serve as one more piece of evidence that Democratic enthusiasm is high in some key states, according to ABC News' analysis.

item.title: Cameroon: Ten years after a massive train disaster, victims are still awaiting justice
item.description: It has been ten years since a Cameroon National Railway Intercity train travelling between Yaounde and Douala derailed and became the country's worst ever railway disaster. Seventy-nine people were killed and hundreds were injured.

item.title: French PM Sebastien Lecornu meets with leaders of political parties amid unrest
item.description: French PM Sebastien Lecornu holds a meeting with the leaders of political parties after unrest this weekend across the country. The aim is to prevent potential violence during the next protests, including on Saturday as the "Yellow vests" movement called for a new mobilisation. Details by FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago.

item.title: Russia agrees to resume trilateral peace talks on Ukraine war
item.description: A US envoy met Putin in Saint Petersburg on Wednesday after the Kremlin agreed to resume peace talks with Ukraine and the United States. Details by FRANCE 24's correspondent Gulliver Cragg.

item.title: Trump ordered to sit for deposition in his $10bn BBC lawsuit
item.description: A federal judge has ordered US President Donald Trump to sit for a deposition in his $10bn defamation lawsuit against the BBC by early December.

item.title: Man charged with murder after woman found dead in car with puncture wounds
item.description: A man has been charged with murder after a housing association worker died following a car crash in South Wales, having sustained "puncture wounds".

item.title: Sir Keir Starmer could be summoned to give evidence to grooming gangs inquiry
item.description: Sir Keir Starmer may be required to give evidence at the grooming gangs inquiry, with hearings due to begin in December.

item.title: Greetings from the Brazil-Argentina border, where waterfalls are flowing at near-record rates
item.description: The Iguazú Falls span more than a mile across both countries. A rain-soaked October, which scientists link to the Super El Niño, has sent near-record volumes of water surging over the towering cliffs.

item.title: Combatting online scams in the age of AI
item.description: One in four Europeans has fallen victim to an online scam, from identity fraud to fake romances. The rise of artificial intelligence is ushering in new risks. Minh Nguyen, Chief Product Officer at security solutions provider Entrust, says both online platforms and governments can play a role in protecting consumers and businesses.

item.title: France: 'Legitimate' grievances over education & inflation risk being overshadowed by violent unrest
item.description: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Dr. Laura Keesman, Assistant Professor of Sociology at the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Dr. Keesman examines the complex relationship between peaceful protest, radical activism, social inequality and state authority. She challenges the tendency to interpret disruptive demonstrations exclusively through the lens of extremism. Even when protesters engage in confrontational or unlawful actions, she argues, their motivations may remain rooted in genuine political and socioeconomic grievances.

item.title: REPLAY: French President vows to prevent violence ahead of protests
item.description: French President ​Emmanuel Macron spoke to the press on Thursday after a meeting with security chiefs. He said that "illegitimate" protests would be banned in ​coming ‌days, ⁠while those from ‌organised groups such as unions ⁠would be offered alternative paths ​for the marches ‌to protect businesses.

item.title: From screen to stage: 'Singin' in the Rain' comes to Paris
item.description: One of the most recognisable and beloved musicals of all time has hit the stage in Paris. "Singin' in the Rain" is on at the Lido theatre until January 10. In this edition of Entre Nous we are pleased to welcome Ashley Day, the British actor bringing Don Lockwood to life. He tells us what it's like to step into Gene Kelly's shoes.

item.title: Brazil's sprawling favelas require long-term urban planning solutions
item.description: As Brazilians head to the polls on Sunday for the second round of presidential elections, our correspondents take us to the heart of the country's favelas, where residents live in unsanitary conditions. Over the past 40 years, the area occupied by Brazilian favelas has almost tripled in size. They now cover around 460,000 hectares, compared with 53,700 in 1985.

item.title: France reports first human case of Shamonda virus, but says there's no public health risk
item.description: France has reported the first-ever recorded case of a human contracting the Shamonda livestock virus, which is most commonly found in cattle. Public health authorities stressed that there did not appear to be any health risk to the public, adding that the infection had been "an exceptional case" involving a person with a severely compromised immune system.

item.title: France bans or curbs protests in bid to prevent new weekend unrest
item.description: French authorities have banned or curbed protests across the country ahead of the weekend in a bid to prevent another wave of the violence and looting that plagued last week’s demonstrations. In Paris alone, hundreds of shops and other small businesses were destroyed on the sidelines of the protests over the cost of living and education funding shortfalls.

item.title: Witkoff lauds 'humanitarian' Putin as Russia releases detained American
item.description: President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff landed in the Russian city of St. Petersburg on Wednesday morning, a Kremlin aide confirmed.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir on how Tampa Bay community came together to repair stadium for Rays
item.description: As the Tampa Bay Rays and their fans prepare for the World Series, David Muir reports on how the community rebuilt the city and repair Tropicana Field after Hurricane Milton.

item.title: Are fresh US-Israeli strikes on Iran in the pipeline?
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Thursday, October 22: The New York Times's sources report plans for fresh strikes on Iran after the US midterm elections. In other news, the French Senate publishes a 30-step proposal for how to "take back control", just days after protests gave way to riots. Also, how software engineers found and patched up bugs in the language that makes up 70 percent of the internet. Finally, the story of a man for whom what happened in Vegas did not stay there.

item.title: Dalai Lama appointed by China 'is going to be a fake one', exiled former Tibetan leader says
item.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, exiled former Tibetan leader Lobsang Sangay said any successor to the Dalai Lama appointed by China "is going to be a fake one". He also likened Beijing's ethnic unity law to "an ethnic erasure", said Tibetan concerns had been "downgraded a bit" in US-China talks and accused China of failing to warn of the deadly August floods on the Nepal-Tibet border.

item.title: Police to close major road near airport as investigation into fatal crash continues
item.description: A major road near Edinburgh Airport will be closed this weekend as part of ongoing investigation work into a fatal crash.

item.title: Two named storms to hit UK on consecutive days
item.description: The second named storm of the season is set to hit the UK on Saturday, the Met Office has said.

item.title: Trump merchandise stores are closing: 'He has peaked'
item.description: At least four Trump merchandise stores have closed this year. Store owners say with Trump in his final term, there isn't as much to fire up his consumer fan base and sales have softened.

item.title: WATCH: 7-year-old singer wins hearts on the street, social media
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to Jordan Sunshine, a boy in California who found therapy for his anxiety by performing on the streets of Los Angeles.

item.title: France reports first Shamonda virus case in human who later died
item.description: The first human case of the Shamonda virus has been detected in France in a person who later died, according to authorities.

item.title: Teacher injured in elementary school shooting says she played dead after being shot
item.description: Becky Drury, a teacher at Silver Rail Elementary School, said her left hand was "almost completely severed" and her right arm was "severely injured."

item.title: Barclays cutting 5,000 jobs in AI-led efficiency drive
item.description: Barclays has revealed it is cutting 5,000 jobs - 5% of its workforce - as part of efforts to save costs and drive efficiency through investment in artificial intelligence (AI).

item.title: North Korea plans to resume propaganda broadcasts along border with South Korea
item.description: North Korea says it plans to resume propaganda broadcasts targeting South Korea within days along the heavily-armed border between the two countries.

item.title: WATCH: American farms honor Dolly Parton with themed corn maze
item.description: Nearly two dozen farms across the country are featuring a Dolly Parton themed corn maze this fall. ABC News' Reena Roy takes us along as she finds her way through one of them in New Jersey.

item.title: 'Millions' of exploitation attempts since security flaw affecting websites emerged
item.description: There have been "millions" of exploitation attempts since a "critical" security flaw affecting websites around the world emerged, according to a major tech company.

item.title: 1800s law must be updated to protect 'backbone' of UK - MP
item.description: An inadequate law from the 19th century must be strengthened to deter saboteurs from attacking the UK's critical undersea cables and pipelines, a minister has said.

item.title: Pope Leo's doctors say tests show he needs no further treatment for lung cancer
item.description: Pope Leo's doctors say final tissue and molecular tests have confirmed his lung cancer was localised, and no further treatment is needed, the Vatican said in a statement.

item.title: WATCH: National Geographic reveals 'Best of the World' destinations
item.description: National Geographic editor-in-chief Nathan Lump talks about must-visit destinations for 2027.

item.title: Supreme Court rebuffs Trump admin restrictions on medical care for trans inmates
item.description: The Supreme Court has rejected a Trump administration appeal seeking to immediately enforce medical care restrictions for transgender people in prison

item.title: PC Sharon Beshenivsky killer jailed over underworld guns operation
item.description: A getaway driver for the gang who shot dead PC Sharon Beshenivsky in an armed robbery has been given a life sentence with a minimum term of eight years over his role in an underworld gun business.

item.title: WATCH: Controversy brews over home of Winnie the Pooh
item.description: ABC News' Danny New examines a controversy about where the stuffed bear that inspired Winnie the Pooh should reside: in England or the New York Public Library?

item.title: WATCH: Hero saves kids on bus
item.description: Surveillance video shows 27-year-old Ebro Ahmed jumping onto a bus to stop it after he noticed the driver having a medical emergency.

item.title: Memorial service held for 'extraordinary' broadcaster Dermot Murnaghan
item.description: A memorial service has been held for former Sky News presenter Dermot Murnaghan, who died in July after a distinguished career at the top of UK journalism.

item.title: WATCH: Pope Leo makes 1st public appearance since surgery
item.description: The pontiff made his way through St. Peter's Square in the Popemobile one week after undergoing lung cancer surgery.

item.title: WATCH: $1 million heist nets rare Pokémon cards
item.description: Nearly $1 million in rare trading cards were stolen from a FedEx truck parked near a Southern California business that authenticates and grades the collectible items, according to police.

item.title: Garda investigation launched as two bodies found in Ireland
item.description: A Garda investigation has been launched after two bodies were discovered in Ireland.

item.title: What workplace violence perpetrators have in common, new Secret Service report finds
item.description: Three quarters of perpetrators who carried out workplace attacks exhibited behaviors of concern: US Secret Service

item.title: At least 153 people killed in drone strike on disputed Sudan-South Sudan region
item.description: A drone strike on a fuel depot in a disputed region on the Sudan-South Sudan border has killed at least 153 people.

item.title: Man arrested in Pakistan over $126m counterfeit postage scheme
item.description: A man has been arrested in Pakistan and accused of running a counterfeit postage operation costing the US Postal Service $126m (£94m).

item.title: Uganda reacts angrily as Nigeria confirms its first Ebola case
item.description: Nigeria has recorded its first case of Ebola during the current outbreak, the country's health ministry has said - as the virus continues to spread internationally.

item.title: WATCH: Great white shark leaps out of ocean off California's Marina Beach
item.description: A great white shark surprised visitors off Marina Beach, California, when it leapt out of the ocean as a beachgoer was taking a video.

item.title: WATCH: Trump says what Russia is doing to Ukraine is 'fine'
item.description: Former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine Bill Taylor reacts to the latest comments from President Donald Trump on Russia as questions grow over America's support of Ukraine.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Swimmer killed in shark attack in South Africa
item.description: A 65-year-old woman was killed in a shark attack at a popular beach on South Africa's southeastern coast, local authorities said.

item.title: WATCH: Funding cuts forcing World Food Program to reduce lifesaving aid in Gaza
item.description: ABC News' Ian Pannell reports on the state of the agency, which says it's been providing food to around 1.6 million people every month since last year's ceasefire announcement.

item.title: Suspect arrested in France after fire at historic city hall
item.description: A man has been arrested after a fire at the town hall of Limoges, according to French media.
